title: Captain Blood

evidence.note: The Catalog of Copyright Entries, Third Series, Parts 12-13 (Motion Pictures and Filmstrips), Jan-Dec 1963, Vol 17 No 1-2, lists a renewal for CAPTAIN BLOOD, a photoplay in twelve reels by Warner Bros. Pictures: original copyright 31DEC35, registration LP6027. It was renewed on 1MAR63 by United Artists Associated, Inc. (PWH) under registration R311594. The twelve-reel length and the 1935 registration date match the 1935 Warner Bros. film. The renewal was filed in the 28th year, so the film's copyright was extended and the print is not public domain.
evidence.source: Catalog of Copyright Entries, Third Series, Parts 12-13, Motion Pictures and Filmstrips, 1963 (archive.org)

evidence.note: This is a sound film, so the recorded track shares the film's own status. The film's copyright was renewed (R311594), so the soundtrack should be treated as protected along with the print. I did not search for separate music registrations.

The film is based on Rafael Sabatini's 1922 novel Captain Blood. Duke CSPD states that the only works clearly in the US public domain as of 2018 are those published before 1923, so the 1922 novel is public domain by term. This covers the novel only, not the 1935 screenplay or the film's own expression.
evidence.source: Duke Center for the Study of the Public Domain, Public Domain Day 2018

editorial:
Captain Blood is Michael Curtiz's 1935 swashbuckler for Warner Bros., with Errol Flynn as Dr. Peter Blood, a physician unjustly convicted of treason who becomes a pirate. It is adapted from Rafael Sabatini's 1922 novel. A creator might want it for its pirate-adventure story and for Flynn's breakout role.

The film is still under copyright. The 1963 Catalog of Copyright Entries records a renewal of the 1935 registration (LP6027), filed 1 March 1963 by United Artists Associated, Inc. as R311594. That means the footage, the recorded soundtrack and the screenplay are protected. The only free layer is the source novel, which was published in 1922 and is public domain by term, so adapt from the book rather than the film.
faq: Can I use clips from the 1935 Captain Blood?

No. The film's copyright was renewed on 1 March 1963 (R311594, United Artists Associated, Inc.), so the footage and soundtrack are protected. Copies on sites such as the Internet Archive are not proof that reuse is allowed.
Can I make my own Captain Blood adaptation?

Yes, from the book. Sabatini's 1922 novel is public domain in the US because it was published before 1923. Do not copy original elements of the 1935 screenplay, such as its scenes, dialogue or visuals.
